clue.text: The very thing!

parts.note: the word 'The' is itself the thing being described: grammar's name for the little word 'the', dressed up as an exclamation of delight

explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'just what I wanted!', but the clue literally names the grammatical class of its own first word.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammarians call 'the' by this name, and the very word 'the' opens the clue.

clue.text: Momentous opening in fuel production

indicators.note: the word 'in' places the opening inside the reworked letters of fuel
a production is something made or staged, so the letters of fuel are reworked

parts.note: a vent is an opening

explanation.surface: A significant gap appears in the manufacture of fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening' reads as part of the surface's start-up of production, but it is a noun giving an outlet, and 'production' is the rearrangement signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A momentous period is one full of important happenings, a synonym.

clue.text: Ruler takes up some followers of Haile Selassie

indicators.note: in a down clue, taking something up reads it from bottom to top, so backwards
only some of the word is used, so its tail is dropped

parts.note: Rastas, Rastafarians, revere Haile Selassie, once called Ras Tafari

explanation.surface: A monarch adopts some of the faithful of the Ethiopian emperor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' trims RASTAS to RAST, and 'takes up' turns that round to give the Russian emperor's title.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsar was the emperor of Russia, so a ruler by example.

clue.text: Standing gets ripe fruit

indicators.note: a fruit is a product or result, so these letters yield something new

explanation.surface: Status comes when fruit has ripened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fruit' looks like the noun the ripeness belongs to, but it signals the rearrangement of GETS RIPE.
explanation.definitionFit: Prestige is high standing or reputation in others' eyes, a synonym.

clue.text: Uriah's reflected about Copperfield's opening lecture

indicators.note: the reflected name goes round, about, the single letter
a reflection shows things backwards, so the name is turned round

parts.note: Uriah Heep is the scheming clerk in Dickens's David Copperfield

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A Dickensian scene: Uriah Heep, mirrored, has his say about the hero's start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflected' makes SPEEH of HEEPS; 'about' puts C, the opening of Copperfield, before the final H.
explanation.definitionFit: A lecture is a formal talk, and a speech is a near synonym.

clue.text: Most holy order works without difficulty

indicators.note: an order puts things in a new arrangement, and works signals it at work on the letters

explanation.surface: A very saintly religious order runs without a hitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' looks like a monastic order, but it signals rearranging MOST HOLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something smoothly means doing it easily, without a hitch: a synonym.

clue.text: Namely — that's right — a Muslim official

parts.note: viz is the abbreviation meaning namely
i.e. stands for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A clarifying aside, set right, introduces an Islamic functionary.
explanation.definitionFit: A vizier was a high official in Muslim states such as the Ottoman Empire.

clue.text: Where one used to Dig for Victory and become competent to tackle danger?

parts.note: VE stands for Victory in Europe
to become competent is to get able

indicators.note: to tackle something is to get to grips with it and work it over, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A wartime home plot, dug for victory, where one learns to face peril.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dig for Victory' was the British wartime campaign urging people to grow their own food; 'to tackle' rearranges DANGER into GARDEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Allotments and home plots for growing produce were where civilians dug during the war.

clue.text: What happens in the fall, without starting to spy

indicators.note: the opening letter is removed, so the phrase loses its start

parts.note: in autumn, the American fall, leaves drop

explanation.surface: Asking what takes place in autumn, minus a beginning, to snoop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fall' is the American word for autumn, when leaves drop.
explanation.definitionFit: To eavesdrop is to listen in secretly, a way of spying.

clue.text: Grain finds one in bewilderment

indicators.note: the word 'in' puts the numeral inside the puzzle word

parts.note: a maze is a state of confusion or bewilderment
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A cereal crop finds itself amid confusion.
explanation.definitionFit: Maize, or corn, is a cereal grain.

clue.text: Locals crossing a road need guts

indicators.note: crossing here means stretched across and around the other pieces

parts.note: a local is a British pub, an inn

explanation.surface: Pub-goers crossing a road need courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Locals' suggests residents, but a local is a British neighbourhood pub; 'guts' wants to mean courage but means entrails.
explanation.definitionFit: Guts and innards are both words for internal organs, synonyms.

clue.text: About a book setter has, arousing feeling

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the book word is reversed

parts.note: a tome is a book, usually a large one
the setter is I, so 'setter has' gives I've

explanation.surface: A crossword compiler owns a volume that stirs emotions.
explanation.definitionFit: Emotive language is meant to stir up feelings, a synonym.

clue.text: Instant — not opening but open to doubt

indicators.note: the first letter, the opening, is left off

parts.note: a jiffy is an instant

explanation.surface: A moment that isn't starting but is uncertain.
explanation.definitionFit: Iffy is slang for doubtful or uncertain.

clue.text: Immerse the hair for treating disease

parts.note: to dip is to immerse briefly

indicators.note: treating something processes it, so the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Advice to dunk your hair as a cure for illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Diphtheria is a serious bacterial infection of the throat, an example of disease.

clue.text: English return in clue for poem

indicators.note: the word 'in' places the piece inside the word clue

parts.note: a return is a go back, a go in reverse: OG

explanation.surface: An English comeback within a crossword hint, offered for verse.
explanation.definitionFit: An eclogue is a short pastoral poem, like Virgil's Eclogues.

clue.text: Does song show elements of commendable quality?

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase, its elements, are shown rearranged as another word

explanation.surface: A question whether a song reveals traces of merit.
explanation.definitionFit: Goodness is the quality of being virtuous or good, a synonym.

clue.text: Spooner's horse is going to get a list of items carried

indicators.note: Rev. Spooner swapped the starts of words, so the first sounds change places

parts.note: a bay is a reddish-brown horse
will expresses the future, is going to

explanation.surface: A horse is about to get a cargo manifest.
explanation.definitionFit: A waybill is a document listing goods carried by a vehicle or ship.

clue.text: Undulating tendency of climbers was about to find direction

indicators.note: the word was goes around, about, the climber

parts.note: vines are climbing plants
S, south, is a compass direction

explanation.surface: Mountaineers were about to find their way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbers' suggests mountaineers but means plants, and 'direction' a sense of purpose rather than a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: Waviness is the state of rising and falling in waves, an undulating quality.

clue.text: Cold blockbusters?

parts.note: tools that literally bust frozen blocks, dressed up as chilly box-office hits

explanation.walkthrough: 'blockbusters' suggests hit films, but read literally means things that break up blocks.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiked tools used by climbers and bartenders to break up frozen blocks.

clue.text: Likely to give an answer, especially in revised version

indicators.note: the word 'in' puts the abbreviation inside the reworked letters
a revised text is altered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A new edition is particularly likely to draw a reply.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone responsive reacts readily and gives answers, a synonym.

clue.text: It's dangerous to be without it

definitions.text: It's dangerous to be without it

parts.words: It's dangerous to be without it
parts.note: a thing whose lack means peril, like protection from harm

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like a warning about something risky, but describes the very protection whose absence is the danger.
explanation.definitionFit: The state of being protected from harm, whose absence is peril.

clue.text: Pen with endless desire for a writer

parts.note: a sty is a pen for pigs

indicators.note: without its end, the last letter goes

parts.note: lust is strong desire

explanation.surface: A pen craving to be used by an author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pen' looks like a writing instrument, matching the definition, but it is a pigpen.
explanation.definitionFit: A stylus is a pointed writing implement, used for writing on wax tablets.

clue.text: First part of 18 held in rubber gloves?

definitions.note: 18 down begins with ICE, and a berg is a mass of floating ice

indicators.note: the letters are held inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Something gripped in rubber gloves.
explanation.definitionFit: A berg is a floating mass of ice, the first part of the 18 down entry.

clue.text: Early days in imagination?

parts.note: fancy is imagination

explanation.surface: Childhood dreams exist only in the imagination.
explanation.definitionFit: Infancy is early childhood, and figuratively the early days of anything.

clue.text: Painter who could be smarter

definitions.meaning: Jean-Marc ... was an eighteenth-century French portrait painter
more neatly dressed, the comparative of natty

explanation.surface: An artist who might be better turned out.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a French Rococo portraitist's surname and the comparative of natty, meaning more stylish.

clue.text: Jazz from New Orleans upriver?

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: the Dart is a river in Devon, England

explanation.surface: Jazz travelling up the Mississippi from New Orleans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upriver' looks like one word of direction; split it into 'up' reversing a 'river', the Dart.
explanation.definitionFit: Trad is traditional jazz in the early New Orleans style.

clue.text: Plant for large numbers round the bend

indicators.note: the word round places the numbers around the bend

parts.note: lots means large numbers
a U-bend, so U for a bend

explanation.surface: A plant for many people going mad.
explanation.definitionFit: The lotus is a water plant, such as the sacred lotus of Asia.

clue.text: Hut, one the French surround, is free

indicators.note: the French pieces go around the hut

parts.note: un is French for one
le is French for the
a shack is a hut

explanation.surface: A hut that a French unit encloses becomes free.
explanation.definitionFit: To unshackle is to set free, the verb sense of freeing.
